name: Pratu’s Kitchen
title: A protein brand needed a storefront as premium as its product
tagline: End-to-end brand and digital product design for a fitness creator’s 35.8K-follower vegetarian food brand, launching in 2026.

heroMedia.alt: The Pratus Kitchen home page: the PRATUS wordmark and ‘Culture that performs’ over a photo of the founder holding a cooler and meal pouches

intro: Pratus Kitchen is a vegetarian, high-protein Indian meal brand, with the tagline “Culture that performs.” I’m directing its end-to-end brand and digital product design: the user journeys, the visual direction, the brand’s design system and the front end.
The direction from the start was clean, professional and premium. Think Nike, not a recipe blog.

sections.label: The product page
sections.heading: Every meal leads with its macros
body: Each meal page puts calories, protein, carbs and fat right under the price, the same numbers that are printed on the pouch.

media.alt: The Push Day Paneer Paratha product page: a photo of the founder flexing with the pouch beside the macros — 470 calories, 30g protein, 29g carbs, 26g fat
media.caption: The paneer paratha page: macros sit above the description, not below it.

sections.label: Shop and account
sections.heading: A full shop, ready for the backend
body: Behind the product pages: a cart, a three-step checkout and an account page with orders, one-tap reorder and a running tally of meals and protein delivered.
Payments, sign-in and real orders connect through a written API contract with the backend developer, so the front end and the backend can be built in parallel.

items.alt: The paneer paratha page on a phone
The account page on a phone, with orders and a reorder button

media.caption: Product and account on a phone.

sections.label: Rounds with the client
sections.heading: Calmer with every round
body: The client asked for flat colour, a calm hero, full-photo cards and a standard two-column product page, so the animated tagline effect came out of the hero.

Some calls were mine. I tried a white About section and kept it dark. Larger how-to icons were too big, so they now sit at the height of the step numbers. On phones the menu stays a compact pill instead of spreading full width.

media.alt: The Pratus Kitchen checkout: three numbered blocks beside a sticky order summary
media.caption: Checkout: three numbered steps and a summary that stays in view.

reflection.label: Where it is now
reflection.heading: Launching in 2026
body: Prices, shipping and the founder’s story are still placeholders waiting on the client, and the backend is being built alongside the front end.
